paper_title: Vector Wave Dark Matter and Terrestrial Quantum Sensors
suggested_experiment_name: Optomechanical cavity B-L vector DM projection (three-peak analysis)
coupling_convention: g_{B-L}, dimensionless U(1)_{B-L} gauge coupling, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 5
notes: Paper (Amaral, Jain, Amin, Tunnell, arXiv:2403.02381) develops a three-peak Fourier-space statistical framework for stochastic vector wave DM and applies it to project 90% CL sensitivities on ultralight B-L gauge boson DM using an optomechanical cavity accelerometer (Fig. 5, curves for f0 = 0.1, 1, 10 Hz; valid mass window 5e-20 eV <~ m <~ 5e-15 eV, Tobs = 10 sidereal days, latitude of Houston). No table of limit values is provided; the data_points above are an APPROXIMATE envelope read from the description of Fig. 5 and should be treated as indicative only (couplings between ~1e-27 and ~1e-25 over the stated mass range), hence the reduced extraction confidence. The only explicit numerical limit in the text is the authors' UPDATED MICROSCOPE (final results) recast: |g_BL| <~ 7e-26 at low masses (a fifth-force bound, not a DM haloscope limit, so no DM density applies to it). DM density: intro states rho ~ GeV/cm^3, and the quoted characteristic acceleration a0 ~ 1e12 m/s^2 is consistent with rho = 1 GeV/cm^3. Signal is a differential acceleration on materials with differential B-L charge Delta_ij ~ 0.1. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('ENVELOPE of the three solid projection curves') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 5 shows 90% CL projected limits on g_{B-L} for an optomechanical cavity with T_obs = 10 T_Earth, for three resonance frequencies f0 = 0.1, 1, 10 Hz. I traced the lower ENVELOPE of the three solid projection curves: f0=0.1 Hz flat at ~1.6e-27 up to its resonance (~4e-16 eV, i.e. 0.1 Hz Compton), then rising steeply; switching to the f0=1 Hz curve near 2e-15 eV (flat ~8.5e-27, dip ~7e-27 near 1e-14 eV); switching to the f0=10 Hz curve near 3e-14 eV (dip ~4.5e-26 near 4.5e-14 eV). Existing bounds shown in grey: Eot-Wash ~3.5e-24 and MICROSCOPE (Final) ~7e-26 (text quotes g_{B-L} < 7e-26 at low masses), used as benchmark calibration. Region above m ~ 5e-15 eV lies in the shaded T_obs > tau_coh zone where the framework is less valid.
